newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada Liberals headed for possible minority.
newsitem.headline: Canada Liberals headed for possible minority.

text.p: Prime Minister Jean Chretien could lose his majority in the Canadian Parliament, television analysts suggested on Monday.
The Global television network projected a minority after Chretien's Liberals were thrashed in Atlantic Canada. CTV Ottawa bureau chief Craig Oliver said: "I think we're looking at a minority."
In Atlantic Canada, the Liberals lost or were projected to lose 22 of the regions's 32 seats, including at least two cabinet ministers.
The Liberals won a 29-seat majority in the last election in 1993 and can ill afford to lose almost two dozen seats in one region alone.

Among those defeated by the leftist New Democratic Party were Defense Minister Doug Young in New Brunswick and Health Minister David Dingwall in Nova Scotia, both of whom were blamed for tough cuts in social programs.

"Evidently, we cannot touch programs without paying the price. Tonight we are being punished because people have the impression that we penalized them over the last two or three years with the changes that were made to employment insurance, but also to other programs," Young told the Canadian Broadcasting Corp.
